attributes.residual: NONE - real 32 -> 0, the largest single closure of this pass. The exit-position update runs three consecutive int-to-float conversions of identical shape: `stw` the integer half to a stack slot, `lfd` the pair back as a double, `fsubs` off the 2^52 bias, then `fmuls`/`fadds`/`stfs` into the player record at 68/72/76(r31). Ours interleaves the three triples one slot differently from the target - four local transpositions, order [0,1,2,3,4,5,9,7,6,8,11,12,10,14,13,15,16,17,18,19,20,21] over +0x1f0..+0x248 - and colours the whole f0/f1 pair the other way round. The audit accepts because no moved atom crosses a store/load pair sharing a slot: the `stw r0,40(r1)`/`lfd 40(r1)` and `stw r4,36(r1)` pairs keep their relative order, and what moves is their interleaving against the independent f3/f4 arithmetic. The 15 remaining rows are the bijective f0<->f1 renaming.
